correctness.rationale: In the left Leibniz algebra [e3,e1]=e1+e2 and [e3,e2]=e2, a general weight-zero RB operator T has third-row constraints h^2=0, g(g+h)=0, so g=h=0 over a field. In char !=2, the b≠0 branch has trace -b, ruling out nilpotency; b=0 reduces the nilpotent branch to a=e=i=0 and cd=0, i.e. the union of two 2D affine planes N1=span(E21,E23), N2=span(E13,E23). Their intersection is span(E23), all nonzero points have rank one and square zero. Every automorphism preserves the derived ideal and centralizes the single Jordan block, yielding G(u,v)=[[u,0,0],[v,u,0],[0,0,1]], u≠0; the stated conjugation action fixes d on N1 and has exactly 2q+1 orbits, with normal forms dE21, dE21+E23, E13. Independent exhaustive 3^9 matrix evaluation over F3 returned exactly 15 nilpotent RB maps, identical to the two planes. Independently enumerated conjugacy orbits for F3/F5/F7, obtaining 7/11/15; derived q-point and zeta formulas symbolically.
